\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ادعى} (iddaʿā)}{ادعى (iddaʿā)}]{\ar{ادعى} (iddaʿā) — to claim}

\label{lesson:AR-C366-iddaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to refute, then the Arabic for to be convinced.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ادعى}}
\textbf{\ar{ادعى}} — \emph{iddaʿā} — \textquotedblleft{}to claim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ادعى} \ar{الرجل} \ar{أنه} \ar{طبيب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iddaʿā ar-rajul annahu ṭabīb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man claimed that he was a doctor.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يدعي}, \emph{yaddaʿī}.

Followed by \ar{أن}. The noun is \ar{ادعاء}, \emph{iddiʿāʾ}, a claim.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ادعى}} (\emph{iddaʿā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-ʿ-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to call, to summon\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to call a thing one's own: to claim.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iddaʿā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iddaʿā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iddaʿā ar-rajul annahu ṭabīb.} — The man claimed that he was a doctor.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to refute, then the Arabic for to be convinced, then say \emph{iddaʿā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ادعى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To claim\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{زعم} (zaʿama)}{زعم (zaʿama)}]{\ar{زعم} (zaʿama) — to allege}

\label{lesson:AR-C366-zaama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be convinced, then the Arabic for to claim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{زعم}}
\textbf{\ar{زعم}} — \emph{zaʿama} — \textquotedblleft{}to allege\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{زعم} \ar{التاجر} \ar{أن} \ar{الساعة} \ar{من} \ar{ذهب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{zaʿama at-tājir anna as-sāʿa min dhahab.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The merchant alleged that the watch was made of gold.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يزعم}, \emph{yazʿum}.

\ar{زعم} suggests the speaker doubts the claim.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{زعم}} (\emph{zaʿama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{z-ʿ-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to assert\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Zaʿama} is a Form I verb; Lane notes that it often marks a claim that may be untrue.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaʿama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaʿama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zaʿama at-tājir anna as-sāʿa min dhahab.} — The merchant alleged that the watch was made of gold.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be convinced, then the Arabic for to claim, then say \emph{zaʿama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{زعم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To allege\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شكك} (shakkaka)}{شكك (shakkaka)}]{\ar{شكك} (shakkaka) — to cast doubt}

\label{lesson:AR-C366-shakkaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to claim, then the Arabic for to allege.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شكك}}
\textbf{\ar{شكك}} — \emph{shakkaka} — \textquotedblleft{}to cast doubt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شكك} \ar{الصحفي} \ar{في} \ar{الأرقام} \ar{الرسمية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shakkaka aṣ-ṣaḥafī fī al-arqām ar-rasmiyya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The journalist cast doubt on the official figures.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشكك}, \emph{yushakkik}.

It takes \ar{في}: \ar{شكك} \ar{في} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شكك}} (\emph{shakkaka}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-k-k}, \textquotedblleft{}to doubt\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II of \emph{shakka}, \textquotedblleft{}to doubt\textquotedblright{}: to make others doubt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to claim, then the Arabic for to allege, then say \emph{shakkaka} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صدق} (ṣaddaqa)}{صدق (ṣaddaqa)}]{\ar{صدق} (ṣaddaqa) — to believe someone}

\label{lesson:AR-C366-saddaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to allege, then the Arabic for to cast doubt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صدق}}
\textbf{\ar{صدق}} — \emph{ṣaddaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to believe someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{يصدق} \ar{أحد} \ar{قصته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam yuṣaddiq aḥad qiṣṣatah.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Nobody believed his story.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصدق}, \emph{yuṣaddiq}.

Form I \ar{صدق}, \emph{ṣadaqa}, with the same letters, means to tell the truth.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صدق}} (\emph{ṣaddaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-d-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to be truthful\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to hold to be truthful: to believe someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaddaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaddaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam yuṣaddiq aḥad qiṣṣatah.} — Nobody believed his story.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to allege, then the Arabic for to cast doubt, then say \emph{ṣaddaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استدل} (istadalla)}{استدل (istadalla)}]{\ar{استدل} (istadalla) — to infer}

\label{lesson:AR-C366-istadalla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to cast doubt, then the Arabic for to believe someone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استدل}}
\textbf{\ar{استدل}} — \emph{istadalla} — \textquotedblleft{}to infer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استدل} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{على} \ar{الزكام} \ar{من} \ar{السعال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istadalla aṭ-ṭabīb ʿalā az-zukām min as-suʿāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor inferred a cold from the cough.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستدل}, \emph{yastadill}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{استدل} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استدل}} (\emph{istadalla}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to guide, to show the way\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to seek guidance: to infer one thing from another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istadalla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istadalla aṭ-ṭabīb ʿalā az-zukām min as-suʿāl.} — The doctor inferred a cold from the cough.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to cast doubt, then the Arabic for to believe someone, then say \emph{istadalla} again
\end{itemize}
